open_points.subject: A18 SQLite-managed files
open_points.text: “The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite”
open_points.question: Which SQLite-created or opened files are covered by this exception: only the main database and rollback journal, or also WAL, shared-memory, statement-journal, temporary and other auxiliary files?
options: Only the main database and rollback-journal files
Every file SQLite opens or creates for this database
open_points.default_guess: Treat every SQLite-managed database or auxiliary file as covered by the exception.

open_points.subject: A18 SQLite journal configuration
open_points.text: “The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite”
open_points.question: Which SQLite journal mode and associated file layout must the store use?
options: Whatever SQLite or the dependency defaults to

open_points.subject: A18 post-start symbolic links
open_points.text: “afterwards only the kernel's user can place one, the directory being private. A link found at start stops the start, and one found later makes that store call fail with nothing written.”
open_points.question: Does the later-link refusal apply to SQLite-managed database and journal paths, and if so, how is it guaranteed across the race between the start walk and SQLite's open when SQLite cannot use `O_NOFOLLOW`?
options: SQLite-managed paths are exempt after the start walk
Same-user replacement is outside the threat model, despite the unconditional invariant
Every SQLite open must be protected by an additional race-free mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Treat same-user replacement as outside the threat model and exempt SQLite-managed opens after the start walk.

open_points.subject: A18 symbolic-link invariant
open_points.text: “symlink_inside(data_directory) -> refused” versus “The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite, which Python cannot ask to refuse a link”
open_points.question: Is the formal invariant intended to cover a database or journal symlink introduced after startup, or must it be narrowed to paths opened by the store itself and links present during the startup walk?
options: It covers every path, including SQLite-managed paths after startup
It covers store-opened paths plus all links present at startup
It covers only files the store opens itself
open_points.default_guess: Narrow it to store-opened paths and links detected by the startup walk.

open_points.subject: A20 unsupported-host startup path
open_points.text: “The kernel does not test the host: on any other the sandbox probe of the start sequence (A03) fails and the start stops” together with “never first asking whether the flag exists and there is no mode without it”
open_points.question: Must the sandbox probe run before any A17 or A18 use of Linux-only `O_NOFOLLOW`, or may an unsupported host stop earlier because that flag or its semantics are unavailable?
options: The sandbox probe must be the first platform-dependent startup action
Any earlier Linux-only failure also counts as the required stopped start
The kernel must explicitly identify and refuse a non-Linux host
open_points.default_guess: Run the sandbox probe before any other Linux-specific startup action and stop on its failure.

open_points.subject: A20 definition of a Linux host
open_points.text: “A release runs on Linux and on no other host. The kernel does not test the host: on any other the sandbox probe of the start sequence (A03) fails”
open_points.question: What determines that a host is non-Linux when a compatibility or virtualization layer can successfully execute the pinned bubblewrap probe, and what enforces the claim that every non-Linux host necessarily fails it?
options: The underlying physical or parent operating system determines the host
The operating-system kernel visible to the process determines the host
Successful execution of the probe itself defines a supported Linux host
open_points.default_guess: Treat the kernel visible to the process as the host and a successful probe as sufficient.
